meta.title: How Do I Get to the Museum?

paragraphs: On Saturday morning, Tom and Lily waited at the bus stop near the market. A woman with a big backpack came to them with a map in her hand. Many people walked past them, and the street was busy. "Excuse me," she said. "I am a tourist, and I am lost." "How can I get to the science museum?" Lily put her finger on the map. "We are here, next to the market," she said. "The museum is in the east of the town."

"Take bus number twelve," said Tom. "It goes east along the river road." "How many stops is it?" asked the woman. "It is six stops," said Lily. "Get off at the stop next to the bridge." "If you get off too early, you will have to walk a long way," said Tom. "Would you show me the bridge on the map?" asked the woman. Tom drew a small circle around it with his pen.

"How long does the bus take?" asked the woman. "It takes about twenty minutes," said Tom. "But at lunchtime there is a lot of traffic, and the bus is slower." "Then I will go now," said the woman. "It is only ten o'clock." "That is a good plan," said Lily. "The bus comes every ten minutes." "Then you can see the whole museum before lunch."

"Can you describe the museum?" asked the woman. "I want to know the building when I see it." "It is a big white building with a round blue roof," said Lily. "There is a tall rocket in front of it." "And there is a small café behind it," said Tom. "That is very clear," said the woman. "I will look for the rocket first."

Bus number twelve came around the corner, and the woman smiled. "You are very helpful," she said. "Thank you, both of you." "You are welcome," said Lily. "Enjoy the museum!" The woman got on the bus and waved from the window. "Our English was good today," said Tom. Lily laughed and said, "And we helped someone, too."
text.summary: A tourist asks Tom and Lily how to go to the science museum by bus. They show her the way on a map, give her the time, and describe the building.
